clinician.final_diagnosis: a ruptured renal AML two weeks after COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old female presented with acute-onset left flank pain, radiating to the left shoulder, and microhematuria, two weeks after a COVID-19 diagnosis. Initial workup showed left CVA tenderness and elevated WBC. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast revealed a ruptured renal AML with moderate left peri-renal hemorrhage. Interventional radiology performed embolization 12 hours after admission, finding no aneurysmal dilatation. Post-procedural course was complicated by continued hemorrhage and retroperitoneal hematoma, leading to a hemoglobin nadir of 6.8 g/dl requiring 2 units of packed red blood cells, and diaphragmatic irritation necessitating supplemental oxygen. On hospital day 6, she developed respiratory COVID-19 symptoms and tested positive again by PCR.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute-onset left flank pain, radiating to left shoulder, and microhematuria.
CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast demonstrated left peri-renal moderate volume hemorrhage with a fat dense lesion in the left kidney (2.5 × 2.3 × 2.1 cm), consistent with ruptured renal AML.
Interventional radiology performed embolization 12 hours after admission.

Post-procedural course was complicated by continued hemorrhage and retroperitoneal hematoma, with a hemoglobin nadir of 6.8 g/dl requiring transfusion of 2 units packed red blood cells, and diaphragmatic irritation requiring supplemental oxygen.
On hospital day 6, she developed respiratory COVID-19 symptoms and again tested positive by PCR assay for COVID-19.
Patient had a known history of COVID-19 diagnosed via nasopharyngeal PCR two weeks prior to presentation.
